pages.text: Cold Sweat tracks two temperatures: the $(bold)air$() where you stand and your $(bold)body$(). The air follows the biome, the season, the hour, altitude, rain and shade. Your body follows the air slowly; the gauge by your hotbar shows which way it is going.$(br2)There is no thirst. Comfortable air is 35 to 110 °F; the thermometer reads it.

Far enough either way and it hurts: the cold slows and freezes you, heat wears you down. New players get a grace period. Winter nights, rain and high ground are the danger.$(br2)The capital sits in mild country: comfortable in spring and autumn, a cold winter, a warm summer. Deserts peak near 95 °F and the Nether is a steady 100 °F: only a high-summer noon, or standing by lava, is too hot.

A lit campfire, fire, furnace, smoker, blast furnace or stove warms you within a few blocks, more the closer you stand. Walls between you and the fire weaken it. Lava and magma are hot; ice cools.$(br2)A roof, four walls and a fire is a winter night survived.
pages.title: Heat

pages.text: The fire drill: three sticks. Hold right-click on a block for two seconds to light a campfire or candle, or start a fire. Twelve uses.
Insulates any armour piece, from any mod. Wool keeps out cold, rabbit hide heat, leather a little of both. Shears take it back off.
Warmed at a campfire: a hot-water bottle. The thermometer reads the air.

The hearth heats a whole house: fuel it and fit a smokestack; pipes carry the air further. The boiler warms a room, the icebox cools one. All three are $(bold)Climate control$(), held by the Frostmaw (Tier 2).
pages.title: Climate control
